title: Bi-stable elements
body:
A **bi-stable element** is a circuit with exactly two stable states, which is the entire
trick behind [[Sequential Logic]]. Cross-couple two inverters (the output of each feeding
the input of the other) and the loop has two configurations it is happy to sit in forever:
$Q=0$ or $Q=1$. Nothing external is holding it there. That is one bit of memory, built out
of nothing but gates.

The catch is that "two stable states" is not the same as "only two states". There is a
third, unstable point halfway between, and a bi-stable element pushed there sits balanced
until noise tips it one way or the other. See [[metastability]].

Every storage circuit in this course is a bi-stable element with extra control wired
around it: [[SR-Latch]], then [[D-Latch]], then [[Flip-Flop]], then [[Shift Register]].
